message.content:
The “best” movie of 2020 depends on what you’re looking for—critical acclaim, audience reception, or cultural impact. Here’s a quick snapshot of the most celebrated films from that year:

| Film | Year‑of‑Release | Critical Consensus | Audience Reception | Notable Awards |
|------|-----------------|---------------------|--------------------|----------------|
| **Parasite** | 2019 (U.S. release 2020) | 98 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 94 % on Metacritic | 8.5/10 on IMDb | Best Picture Oscar (2020), Best International Feature |
| **Nomadland** | 2020 | 97 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 92 % on Metacritic | 8.2/10 on IMDb | Best Picture Oscar (2021), Best Director (2021) |
| **Soul** | 2020 | 95 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 90 % on Metacritic | 8.3/10 on IMDb | Best Animated Feature Oscar (2021) |
| **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | 2020 | 93 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 88 % on Metacritic | 7.9/10 on IMDb | Best Original Screenplay Oscar (2021) |
| **1917** | 2019 (U.S. release 2020) | 94 % on Rotten Tomatoes, 91 % on Metacritic | 8.3/10 on IMDb | Best Cinematography Oscar (2020) |

### Why “Parasite” Often Tops the List

- **Universal acclaim**: It’s the only film to receive a perfect score on Rotten Tomatoes’ “Certified Fresh” list for 2020.
- **Cultural impact**: The film sparked global conversations about class, family, and capitalism.
- **Awards**: It won the Academy Award for Best Picture, becoming the first non‑English‑language film to do so.

### If You Prefer a 2020‑Only Release

- **Nomadland**: A quiet, contemplative look at modern American nomads that won Best Picture at the Oscars the following year.
- **Soul**: A Pixar masterpiece that blends music, philosophy, and animation, winning Best Animated Feature.

### Bottom Line

If you’re looking for the most critically lauded film that also had a huge cultural footprint, **“Parasite”** is the clear winner. If you want a film that was released in 2020 and still received top honors, **“Nomadland”** is your best bet. Both films offer distinct storytelling styles and have earned their places in cinematic history.
